english: Two players $A$ and $B$ share a ball, which is with $A$ at time $t=0$. At each of the times $t=1,2,3,\dots$, whoever holds the ball keeps it with probability $\dfrac45$ and passes it to the other player with probability $\dfrac15$, independently of all earlier times. For each positive integer $n$, let $p_n$ and $q_n$ denote the probabilities that the ball is with $A$ and with $B$, respectively, just after time $t=n$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(p_n-q_n\right)$ is ______.
hindi: दो खिलाड़ी $A$ तथा $B$ एक गेंद साझा करते हैं, जो समय $t=0$ पर $A$ के पास है। प्रत्येक समय $t=1,2,3,\dots$ पर, जिसके पास गेंद है वह उसे प्रायिकता $\dfrac45$ से अपने पास रखता है तथा प्रायिकता $\dfrac15$ से दूसरे खिलाड़ी को दे देता है, सभी पूर्ववर्ती समयों से स्वतन्त्र रूप से। प्रत्येक धनात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए माना $p_n$ तथा $q_n$ क्रमशः वे प्रायिकताएँ हैं कि समय $t=n$ के ठीक बाद गेंद $A$ के पास तथा $B$ के पास है। तब $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(p_n-q_n\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: The ball is with $A$ after time $n+1$ if it was with $A$ and was kept (probability $\frac45$), or was with $B$ and was passed (probability $\frac15$). So $p_{n+1}=\dfrac45p_n+\dfrac15q_n$ with $q_n=1-p_n$, i.e. $p_{n+1}=\dfrac15+\dfrac35p_n$, and $p_0=1$.

The fixed point of $x\mapsto\dfrac15+\dfrac35x$ is $x=\dfrac12$. Subtracting it: $p_{n+1}-\dfrac12=\dfrac35\left(p_n-\dfrac12\right)$, so $p_n-\dfrac12$ is a geometric progression with first value $p_0-\dfrac12=\dfrac12$ and ratio $\dfrac35$.
originality_note: New: a two-state passing process whose probability p_n satisfies a linear recurrence; the difference p_n - q_n is a pure GP and the infinite series of these differences is asked (way 5: probability recursion linked with an infinite GP). Closest known: 'random walk on the vertices of a triangle / probability of an even number of heads in n tosses'. Different because: the quantity is the infinite sum of the holding advantage p_n - q_n, which needs the closed form and then a GP sum.

concept_use.Sequences defined by a recurrence relati: p_{n+1} = 1/5 + (3/5)p_n is solved for the n-th term p_n = 1/2 + (1/2)(3/5)^n.
concept_use.Probability problems requiring recursion: The recursion comes from conditioning on who holds the ball, and the infinite series sum of (3/5)^n gives 1.5.
